text: . In Men’s cricket, India crushed the West Indies by eight wickets in the second ODI of the three-match series at Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati last night, taking an unassailable 2-nil lead.Put into bat, West Indies posted their highest-ever ODI total of 405 for seven, powered by centuries from John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo.In reply, India comfortably chased down the target in 43.3 overs, losing only two wickets. Captain Shubman Gill led the charge with a sensational unbeaten 233 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 balls to register his 35th ODI century.The Indian opening pair put on a record-breaking 255-run partnership for the first wicket. Gill also became the fastest player to score a double century in ODI cricket, reaching the landmark in just 117 balls, while his unbeaten 233 became the highest individual score by an Indian in an ODI run chase. Gill was named Player of the Match for his outstanding innings.India had also won the opening ODI in Thiruvananthapuram by eight wickets. The third and final match of the series will be played on Saturday in New Chandigarh.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat programme appreciated Hockey Olympian from Punjab, Rajinder Singh Senior for his efforts to discover and coach sports talent from the villages of the state.Lauding him for pursuing his passion through the Round Glass Hockey Academy to train children in hockey in villages, the prime minister said that Mr Rajinder has a very clear focus in identifying children that lack access to excellent coaching facilities at village level.Akashvani correspondent reports that Olympian Rajinder Singh was part of the gold medal-winning Indian hockey team at the 1980 Olympics. He played his last international match in the 1982 Champions Trophy, which India won from Pakistan and got a Bronze medal with him converting three penalty corners into goals.He joined the Sports Authority of India in 1990 and started his coaching career.During his tenure, the sub-junior and Junior Hockey Teams achieved many national awards. After his retirement from SAI, this Dronacharya awardee joined Round Glass Sports Academy in 2020 and started nurturing young talent from villages to make them national-level players.He told Akashvani that at present, the academy is running 60 Hockey academies in Punjab, in which 3000 budding players, including girls between 6 to 8 age groups are learning the nuances of this National sport.The Olympian, who is fulfilling his passion, thanked the Prime Minister for appreciating his efforts and said that his inspirational words would not only inspire him to work with more vigor but inspire other coaches also. He assured to continue coaching the young talent to build a strong hockey team for India.

. The co-pilot accused of assaulting Captain Smit Machchhar has been transferred to Abu Dhabi. The Saudi Press Agency (SPA), quoting an official source at the Saudi Ministry of Interior, reported that both pilots left the country for Abu Dhabi after receiving medical clearance.The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi had yesterday informed that Captain Machchhar had been brought to the UAE and was recovering well. As reported by SPA, the aircraft landed safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk at 9:45 a.m. on Wednesday, with 174 passengers and an eight-member crew, all of whom received necessary logistical and medical assistance.At 5:40 p.m., passengers continued their journey on a replacement flydubai aircraft, while the crew returned to Dubai on a separate flight.The captain and co-pilot were taken to a local hospital for medical evaluation and treatment.Following medical clearance, both pilots departed Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on Thursday, accompanied by the UAE security team. According to SPA, preliminary investigations by Saudi authorities, in coordination with a UAE security team, revealed that an altercation occurred in which the co-pilot assaulted the captain, resulting in injuries to both individuals.

. Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has very good ideas aimed at finding a mutually acceptable solution to the Ukraine conflict.Speaking at the Valdai Forum, Mr Putin noted that Mr Modi regularly raises the topic of ending the war during their discussions and shows strong interest in a peaceful settlement.Mr Putin described India’s diplomatic position as neutral yet deeply invested in bringing the hostilities to an end, while Mr Modi has previously emphasised that India stands firmly “on the side of peace”.Mr Putin expressed gratitude for Mr Modi’s persistent engagement and practical approach toward dialogue and diplomacy.

. Captain Smit Machchhar, who was injured in the flydubai flight incident, is in stable condition and recovering well, said India’s Ambassador to the UAE, Dr Deepak Mittal.Speaking Exclusively to Akashvani News, Ambassador Mittal said he met Captain Machchhar and his family in the UAE and found the pilot in good spirits. Mr Mittal said Smit was speaking openly, smiling and laughing, which was a great relief for us and, most importantly, for his family.Dr Mittal said the Captain is receiving good medical care and that the Indian Embassy remains in continuous contact with the UAE authorities. He added that the Embassy would ensure that Captain Machchhar receives the best possible medical care and all assistance available for his recovery.

. The Supreme Court will tomorrow hear a plea challenging the Centre’s decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified UPI person-to-merchant transactions of over 2,000 rupees.Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI payments, the government has introduced a 0.4 per cent fee on transfers of over 2,000 Rs made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge. The MDR will be capped at 300 Rs for payments of 75,000 Rs and above.Essential and thin-margin sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs — will pay a flat MDR of 5 Rs per transaction above 2,000 Rs.Payments into mutual funds, securities and through stockbrokers and dealers will attract 0.02 per cent MDR, also capped at 300 Rs. Bench of Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the plea.The Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Anjan Datta has challenged the Centre’s decision. The plea alleged that the levy has been introduced without adequate statutory safeguards, transparency or public consultation.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices witnessed a sharp decline and were trading around 1.3% lower during the afternoon session. The Sensex tumbled 956 points to 72,939, while the Nifty shed 306 points to 22,835 when reports last came in.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 1.4%, while the Smallcap 100 index slid 1.6% a short while ago. On the sectoral front, all sectors were trading in the red, as a broad-based sell-off was seen across the board.

. At the Asian Games 2026, India’s compound mixed archery team of Sahil Jadhav and Chikitha Taniparthi has won a gold medal, beating Korea in a shoot-off in the finals. The Indian duo also secured a 2028 Olympic quota place with this win. They defeated Thailand in the Semi-finals.Earlier, the Indian Women’s Compound Archery team clinched gold after beating China 238-234 in the finals today at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park, Japan. The Indian team, comprising Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, entered the finals after beating South Korea 234-233 in the semifinals. India won gold in the Women’s compound team event at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou. India now has a total of 54 medals, including eight gold, 21 silver and 25 bronze medals.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Indian compound archer Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru produced a commanding performance to win the men’s individual bronze medal at the Asian Games here today. Ganesh, who was a part of the gold-winning men’s team yesterday, defeated Vietnam’s Cong Duc Dang 149-144 in the bronze medal playoff after bowing out of individual gold contention with a semifinal loss.In squash, India settled for a bronze medal after losing 1-2 to Hong Kong in the women’s team semifinal. Meanwhile, in sepaktakraw, India assured itself of at least a bronze medal after defeating Vietnam 2-nil in the men’s quadrant event to advance to the semifinals.India were assured of a medal in the Asian Games sepaktakraw men’s quadrant competition after the team entered the semifinals with a 2-1 win over Myanmar, keeping an unbeaten run intact to top group A today.India also opened its sailing medal account at the Asian Games as Manu Francis and Prince Kurisinkal Noble secured silver in the men’s skiff competition today, finishing behind China after nine races.Meanwhile, in Men’s cricket, India trounced Sri Lanka by 124 runs to set up a high-voltage final against Pakistan.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today spoke to brave Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, whose heroics in thwarting an attack by his co-pilot saved 180 lives on the flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Captain Machchaar gave details of his experience to the Prime Minister and spoke of what gave him courage during the incident. The Prime Minister applauded his bravery and wished him a quick recovery.

. India’s Women’s Squash team reached the Asian Games semifinals with a 2-0 win over Singapore today, assuring a medal for the country. Tanvi Khanna beat Au Yeong Wai Iynn 11-6, 4-11, 15-13, 11-1 before Anahat Singh defeated Au Yeong Wai Yhann 11-7, 11-3, 11-4. Veteran Joshna Chinappa did not need to play. India will face its Semifinal opponent at Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena tomorrow. India had topped Pool C after wins over China, Japan and Iran.In Men’s Greco-Roman Wrestling, Sunil Kumar advanced to the Semifinals of 87 kg category today after defeating Tajikistan’s Muhammad Sultonzoda 9-0 by technical superiority in the first period. The 2023 Hangzhou bronze medalist dominated the bout and sealed victory with consecutive gut-wrench moves after Sultonzoda was placed in the par terre position. Sunil is likely to face Japan’s Taizo Yoshida in the Semifinals. However, in the Women’s 68 kg round of 16, Nisha Dahiya lost to North Korea’s Pak Sol Gum.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.
. Greco Roman wrestler Nitesh Siwach today bagged silver medal in men’s 97kg at Asian games in Japan. Nitesh lost to Japan’s Yuri Nakazato 0-4 in the final.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have offloaded Indian equities worth 17,131 crore rupees in September so far. According to the latest depository data, out of the total net outflows, 25,682 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market has continued this month, with FPIs infusing 8,551 crore rupees in the primary market in September so far.Meanwhile, Foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. In September so far, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 7,385 crore rupees. FPIs have withdrawn 3,021 crore rupees through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR) and 1,889 crore rupees through the General Limit route.

At least nine Afghan civilians, including women and children, were killed and 11 others injured in Pakistani airstrikes on civilian homes in Afghanistan’s Kunar and Helmand provinces, according to Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid. He said the strikes yesterday also destroyed three residences in the Shultan district of Kunar and Garmser district of Helmand.The latest attacks come amid an escalation in Pakistani airstrikes across several Afghan provinces. Mujahid said four civilians were killed in strikes in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost on September 24, while three people were killed in attacks in Kunar and Paktika three days earlier.Condemning the latest strikes as an act of aggression, Mujahid accused Pakistan of using attacks on Afghanistan to divert attention from domestic political and economic problems. He also warned that Afghanistan would give an “appropriate response” to what he described as Pakistani military aggression.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 8% year-on-year in August this year. The latest data indicate that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, with the upward revision in July’s IIP growth to 7.4% from the earlier estimate of 6.7%.According to government data released today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 12.3% in August, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 9%. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 6.3%. However, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 5.6% during the period under review.

. Israeli Prime Minister’s spokesperson David Mencer has said that Flydubai hijack attempt seemed similar to 9/11 terror attacks in the United States. Talking to a news agency, he said, the Omani pilot after attacking brave Indian pilot Smit Machchhar in yesterday’s Flydubai flight was found standing over the cockpit controls trying to destroy the aircraft’s systems. Mencer said, the attempt to bring down the flight seemed similar to the September 11 attacks.He said, the Omani pilot is being questioned by the Saudi authorities and he will be transferred to the UAE. He added that Israel and the UAE have instituted a six-day freeze on flights between the two countries to investigate the incident and ensure there are no follow-up attacks. Mencer mentioned that the Israeli passengers and crew, together with the Indian pilot wrestled control of the plane back from the Omani pilot and brought the incident to a safe conclusion.

. The United States has imposed sanctions on 10 individuals and entities across several countries for allegedly helping procure weapons and military components for Iran’s Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL). In a report, The Media Line says that among those sanctioned is a Pakistani businessman along with three companies linked to the person.Moreover, the businessman is chairman of the Pakistan-based Cavalier Group, a private defence company with operations in Pakistan and other countries. In addition, US authorities allege that the person and the company acted as intermediaries for Iran’s defence ministry and helped facilitate the procurement and distribution of weapons.Apart from that, the US action against Saudi Arabia-based Cavalier Dynamics for Technologies was carried out in coordination with Saudi authorities. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, Washington would continue targeting individuals and entities that provide support to Iran under Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign launched in August to disrupt the Iranian regime’s economic networks.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has highlighted India’s food security measures and reaffirmed commitment to rules-based multilateral trading system. Participating in the opening day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Mr Goyal thanked the US G20 Presidency for placing food at the centre of the discussions. He said that ensuring food security for all and creating greater opportunities for farmers are central to India’s policy. He reiterated that food must never be used as an instrument of pressure against any country.Mr Goyal pointed out that countries of the Global South are among the most adversely impacted by the food, fuel and fertiliser crises caused by global conflicts. He stressed that today’s fertiliser shortage could become tomorrow’s food crisis. The Ministers reached consensus on the outcome document, ‘G20 Statement on the Weaponization of Food through Coercive Trade Actions’, and expressed their intent to continue cooperation on the subject.Earlier in the day, Mr Goyal joined G20 Trade Ministers and Ambassador Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative, on a visit to the Rockwell Automation office and factory in Mequon, Wisconsin. The Minister also held bilateral meetings with Trade Ministers and Representatives of Key G20 Partners on Sidelines of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting.

. The Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) has initiated a series of reforms to make aviation security processes simpler and quicker for the people working at Indian Airports.Briefing the media on the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) Reforms to Improve Operational Efficiency and Ease of Doing Business in New Delhi, Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha said that these sweeping changes aim to digitise workflows, making processes simpler, and transition towards accountability-driven governance while maintaining the highest security standards.The Ministry informed that BCAS has streamlined the security clearance framework by moving towards a category-and contract-agnostic security clearance which is applicable across the nine identified categories of aviation entities.It is proposed to remain valid for five years as part of these reforms. BCAS has also introduced a more structured and time-bound approach to security vetting of airport infrastructure.It emphasises obtaining and communicating all necessary clarifications at one stage, prescribed timelines at different stages and closer monitoring of pending cases.To transform the Aerodrome Entry Permit system the BCAS has initiated an end-to-end digital workflow to streamline the entire process.The system provides for online registration and application, document submission, digital scrutiny and verification, defined approval workflows and digital issuance, with facial biometric verification. The system is being implemented as a common platform across all 169 airports.The Ministry highlighted that these reforms are essential, as Indian has become world’s third-largest domestic aviation market with number of operational airports has grown from 74 in 2014 to 165 in July 2026.It has added that these reforms are part of the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and the effort to build a future-ready aviation security regulatory framework that can keep pace with a rapidly expanding aviation sector.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices declined sharply by over 1.5% today. The Sensex plunged 1,240 points to close at 72,772. The Nifty shed 360 points to settle at 22 thousand 780. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index tumbled 1.6%, while the Smallcap 100 index tanked 1.8%.In the Sensex pack, 29 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses, with Infosys emerging as the lone gainer, rising 0.2%. Among the top underperformers, Larsen and Toubro slumped 2.8%, PowerGrid declined 2.6%, and Adani Ports fell 2.4%.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged lower. Among the top laggards,PSU Banks skidded 3.2%, Power, Telecommunication, and Utilities lost 2.3% each and Mid-Small Private Banks dropped 2.2%.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 3218 companies declined, 1271 advanced and 228 remained unchanged.

. India’s men’s squash team bagged the bronze medal at the Asian Games 2026 as they lost 1-2 to Malaysia in the semifinal at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan today.The men’s squash team’s bronze came after the Indian women’s team also lost 1-2 to Hong Kong in the semifinal to secure a bronze medal on the same day. The men’s team’s bronze medal in squash took India’s medal tally to five on Day 12 of the Asian Games today. India’s medal tally has risen to 65, including 10 gold, 23 silver and 32 bronze medals. Currently, India is at 8th position.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices extended their losing streak for the fourth straight day today. The Sensex plunged 571 points or 0.8 per cent to close at 71,910. The Nifty shed 199 points or 0.9 per cent to settle at 22,422.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 as well as the Smallcap 100 indices tumbled one per cent each.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave will be held from this Saturday in New Delhi, under the theme of ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’. The Ministry of Finance said that the three-day gathering will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries.The Ministry added that the Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment. The Ministry said that these roundtables will provide opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address on the first day of the conclave. The conclave will also witness addresses from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and other Union Ministers. The Ministry informed that the conclave will also feature a special address by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. Saudi Arabia has handed over to UAE, the Omani co-pilot who made an abortive attempt to crash Flydubai’s Tel Aviv bound plane. Investigators are probing the attack on Indian pilot Smit Machchhar by the Omani co-pilot in the cockpit.The development came after Saudi authorities conducted a preliminary investigation into the incident, that forced the flight to make an emergency landing in the Saudi city of Tabuk on Wednesday.Saudi Arabia’s Interior Ministry said its initial investigation indicated that the co-pilot has assaulted the captain during the flight. The preliminary investigation was conducted in coordination with security teams from the UAE.Investigations into the incident, which occurred while the plane was flying over Saudi Arabia, are still in their early stages. However, the possibility of a terror motive has heightened concerns in a region already on edge amid the ongoing war with Iran.

. Indian athletes continued their strong performance at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, winning several medals across multiple sporting events today.In Boxing, Lovlina Borgohain clinched a historic gold medal in the women’s 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-nil decision in the final. It is India’s second gold medal in women’s boxing at the Asian Games, following Mary Kom’s gold in 2014.Earlier, India’s women’s recurve archery team created history by winning its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final.India also secured a silver medal in the mixed recurve team archery event. The Indian duo of Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after losing 3-5 to China in a closely contested final.In sailing, Nethra Kumanan won the bronze medal in the women’s dinghy event. The 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with overall 14 points.With these performances, India climbed to sixth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally rose to 70 medals, comprising 12 gold, 24 silver and 34 bronze.President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have congratulated Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma on winning the Bronze Medal in the Women’s Skiff event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, President Murmu said that this medal is a recognition of their efforts and dedication to the sport.Prime Minister Modi said that with determination and consistency, Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma have taken India onto the podium and also improved on the previous performance.

. On the occasion of International Day of Older Persons 2026, a program was organized at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre. Lectures and street plays were arranged in the Cultural Centre to raise awareness about health-related issues concerning older persons and their overall health and well-being.This year’s theme for International Day of Older Persons is The Age of Longevity: Rethinking Systems for Longer Lives. UN Secretary General Antonnio Guterres, in his message, said that elders are leaders and caregivers, who play a vital role in families, communities and economies.The Day calls on Governments, civil society, the private sector, researchers and older persons themselves to examine how societies can ensure that the additional years gained translate into healthy, productive, dignified and equitable lives for all.

. At the Asian Games 2026, India enjoyed another action-packed day in Japan today with the men’s Hockey and Cricket teams reaching their respective finals.The men’s hockey team defeated their arch-rivals Pakistan 4-3 in a thrilling semifinal, while the cricket team beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs to book a place in the gold-medal match. Greco Roman wrestler Nitesh Siwach today bagged  silver medal in men’s 97kg at Asian games in Japan. Nitesh lost to Japan’s Yuri Nakazato 0-4 in the final.Nitesh missed out on a historic gold but secured India’s first silver medal in Greco-Roman wrestling at the Asian Games since 1962.Indian pair of Manu Francis and Prince Kurisinkal Noble bagged the silver medal in the men’s skiff opening race 9 of the Asian Games sailing competition. It is India’s first sailing medal of the Asian Games.The team of Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma won the bronze medal in the women’s skiff sailing event. Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru got bronze in individual compound archery. The men’s and women’s squash teams, also settled for bronze after suffering semifinal defeats.India’s medal tally has risen to 66, including 10 gold, 23 silver and 33 bronze medals.

. The All India Consumer Products Federation and the All India Mobile Retailers Association have decided to withdraw their proposed call for a ‘No UPI Day’ on Friday.The decision was taken following a meeting between a delegation of around 20 senior trade leaders, led by BJP MP and Secretary General of the Confederation of All India Traders, Praveen Khandelwal, and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi. During the meeting, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman assured the delegation that the government remains committed to promoting digital transactions while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders.The trade leaders reiterated their full support for the Digital India mission and the success of UPI, which has emerged as a global model for digital payments. The delegation expressed confidence that continued dialogue between the government and trade bodies would help evolve a practical and sustainable framework to further strengthen India’s digital economy.

. Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu has said Canada wants to support India’s economic growth through deeper cooperation in energy, critical minerals and aerospace.Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Sidhu said India’s growing energy requirements and efforts to diversify supply chains offer significant opportunities for both countries.Sidhu said India and Canada aim to increase bilateral trade from around 30 billion dollars to nearly 70 billion dollars within five years.He said the fifth round of negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement will begin in Ottawa on Monday, with both sides looking to conclude the talks in the coming months.He also highlighted Canada’s potential as a major LNG and critical minerals supplier to India, particularly for electric vehicles and batteries.The minister said the economic partnership should extend beyond trade to investments, research and collaboration.He said Canada welcomes Indian investment in its mining and energy projects, while Canadian companies are already involved in infrastructure projects in India.The two countries have completed four rounds of negotiations and are working towards concluding the trade agreement by the end of 2026.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. India enjoyed its most successful day at the ongoing Asian Games in Japan so far, winning four gold medals today. The country completed a hat-trick of gold medals in compound archery, with the women’s team, mixed team and men’s team all finishing on top. India also struck gold in shooting, with the mixed trap team securing the top spot. Indian boxers added two more bronze medals to the tally, with Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya finishing on the podium today. Boxer Narendra Berwal had bagged the bronze yesterday.Later in the day, Wrestler Sunil Kumar won bronze in the men’s 87kg Greco-Roman event, beating the Philippines’ Callum Johnston Roberts 9-nil. Kumar, who also won bronze at Hangzhou 2022, became the first Indian wrestler to win multiple Greco-Roman medals at the Asian Games.In Women’s Hockey, India defeated South Korea 2-nil this evening to reach the final. Ishika Chaudhary and Captain Salima Tete scored for India. India will face defending champions China in final on Friday. India are now just a victory away from securing its only second Asian Games women’s hockey gold medal, with their only previous triumph coming way back in 1982.In Squash, India’s Men’s and Women’s teams advanced to the semifinals, assuring two more medals. The top-seeded and defending champion Men’s team beat Kuwait 2-Nil, while the Women’s team defeated Singapore by the same margin. India have already won two Singles silver medals in Squash through Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh, and a mixed doubles bronze through Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar.With these victories, India’s medal tally has risen to 60, including 10 gold, 21 silver and 29 bronze medals.

The National Statistics Office (NSO), is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026.The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said that the survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises. The Ministry added that the survey will provide important inputs for understanding emerging investment trends in the Indian economy.The primary objective of the CAPEX Survey is to collect information on capital expenditure undertaken in the recent financial years , provisional capital expenditure in the current financial year and investment intentions for the forthcoming financial year.The Ministry has appealed all the selected private corporate sector enterprises to extend their full cooperation and participate actively in the CAPEX 2026 Survey.

India’s registered manufacturing sector recorded strong growth in financial year 2025 (FY25), with industrial output rising 7.81 per cent and total employment increasing almost 7.2 per cent over the previous year.According to the Annual Survey of Industries data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today, the total number of establishments in this sector increased from 2.60 lakh in FY24 to 2.67 lakh in FY25, representing a growth of 2.64 per cent. The highest number of establishments was reported in Tamil Nadu, followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra.Meanwhile, total emoluments paid to the workforce also increased by over 12 per cent in 2024-25 on an annual basis. Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana have emerged as the top 5 states in employment, having a share of more than 56 per cent of the total manufacturing employment of the country in FY25.

. The Nation pays homage to the Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary today. A Sarva Dharma Prarthana Sabha was held at Bapu’s Samadhi, Rajghat in the National Capital.President Droupadi Murmu attended the Sarva Dharma Prarthana this morning and paid floral tributes to the Father of the Nation.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal, and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta also paid tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat.On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that Mahatma Gandhi’s entire life is a beacon of truth, non-violence, compassion, and service.Sharing a social media post, Mr Modi noted that Bapu’s ideals will continue to pave the way for humanity in every era. He wished that the timeless message of Mahatma Gandhi keep guiding the countrymen towards a better society and a Viksit Bharat.The Nation also pays homage to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri on his 122nd birth anniversary today. He was born on 2nd October 1904 in Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Nagar, previously known as Mughalsarai in Uttar Pradesh.As a teenager, he joined India’s freedom struggle and participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1921. Following Independence, Shastri held several important positions in Uttar Pradesh and later in the Union Government.Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid floral tribute to the former Prime Minister at his memorial, Vijay Ghat in the national capital this morning.Delhi Traffic Police has issued a traffic advisory in view of Gandhi Jayanti at Rajghat and the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri at Vijay Ghat today.The Traffic Police informed that Special traffic arrangements will be in place in and around Rajghat, Ring Road and adjoining roads to facilitate the programme ensure smooth and safe movement of traffic and pedestrians. The traffic police informed that traffic may be regulated or diverted between 5 am and 11 am in the morning today.The affected routes include Ring Road: Rajghat to Salim Garh Y-Point towards ISBT Kashmirir Gate, Nishad Raj Marg and Raja Ram Kohli Marg.The traffic police advised the citizens to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional travel time. It also advised them to avoid the affected roads and stretches wherever possible prefer Delhi Metro and other public transport.

NITI Aayog Member Rajiv Gauba today highlighted the critical role of regulation, market-oriented reforms and institutional capacity in strengthening India’s energy security and supporting the country’s journey towards Viksit Bharat at 2047. He noted that the petroleum and natural gas sector operates in an increasingly complex global environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, supply disruptions, and heightened energy-security risks.He said that the creation of PNGRB in 2006 was an important institutional step to ensure fair competition, investor confidence and protect consumer interests. He highlighted PNGRB’s contribution to building the regulatory architecture for natural gas pipelines and noted that its common carrier and contract carrier principles have helped ensure open access to pipeline infrastructure, facilitating greater competition in the downstream market. Mr Gauba emphasised that such regulatory work, while often not visible, is essential for creating predictable markets, building investor confidence and strengthening public trust.Mr Gauba underlined that India’s growing energy requirements make diversification and expansion of domestic energy capacity important elements of the country’s long-term strategy. He also emphasised the importance of accelerating India’s transition towards a gas-based economy.

UAE Attorney-General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi has ordered the formation of an investigation team to probe the incident, including any possible connection to terrorist activity or intent, involving Flydubai flight FZ1073 that forced the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. According to the UAE’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the team, comprising specialised members of the Public Prosecution, will investigate the circumstances and causes of the incident.The Ministry affirmed that the UAE’s judicial authorities have jurisdiction to investigate the incident under applicable legislation, as the aircraft is registered in the UAE and bears its flag. It said that the investigation includes examining all circumstances and motives surrounding the incident, including any possible connection to terrorist activity or intent, and whether it involved prior planning or direction.The UAE appreciated Saudi Arabian authorities for their cooperation and handling of the incident. The Flydubai flight was heading from Dubai to Israel’s Tel Aviv yesterday when the co-pilot tried to sabotage the aircraft and stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar, who was trying to prevent him from doing so. At the time, the Boeing 737, cruising at about 34,000 feet, began dropping at roughly 23,000 feet per minute before reaching about 15,600 feet. However, Smit Machchhar fought back the co-pilot, resisted him, and opened the cockpit door so that passengers and crew members could overpower him. The flight made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk. Earlier in the day, India’s Ambassador to the UAE, Deepak Mittal, visited the family of Captain Smit Machchhar in Dubai and assured them of the Indian government’s full support and assistance.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant today said that technology must be harnessed to make justice more accessible, transparent and responsive, while ensuring that constitutional values and the human character of adjudication remain protected.Addressing the opening session and plenary of the Seventh Congress of the Association of Asian Constitutional Courts and Equivalent Institutions in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, the CJI said the Congress provides an important platform for Asian constitutional courts to exchange experiences and develop principles suited to a common technological future. He said digitalisation can improve access to courts, reduce delays and simplify procedures, while Artificial Intelligence can assist judges and court staff in research and handling large volumes of information.The CJI emphasised that constitutional courts must remain anchored to the principles of dignity, equality, liberty and fairness. He said the challenge is not to choose between tradition and technology, but to bring the best of technology into judicial institutions while keeping the Constitution as the guiding framework.Speaking on the theme of digitising justice, the CJI said the Supreme Court of India’s approach is based on three constitutional promises-liberty under Article 21, equality before law under Article 14, and access to justice through Article 32 and free legal aid under Article 39A. He said digitisation is being treated not merely as computerisation, but as an opportunity to re-engineer judicial processes around citizens.He highlighted the eCourts Mission Mode Project, launched in 2011, under which electronic filing, virtual hearings, digital case management and live-streaming have expanded access to justice. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Supreme Court alone conducted more than seven lakh fifty thousand hearings through video conference between March 2020 and June 2024.The CJI outlined four major initiatives of the Indian Judiciary. These include SUVAS, an AI-assisted translation tool through which more than 83 thousand judgments had been translated into 18 Indian languages; Su-Sahayak, an AI-powered chatbot providing case status, cause lists, orders, judgments and e-services guidance; and One Case, One Data, which integrates case information across different levels of the judiciary to reduce duplication and delay.He also referred to the Supreme Court AI Committee’s Draft Regulations for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Courts, released in June this year. He stressed that the regulations are based on the principle of human primacy, with AI supporting judicial research and court processes but never replacing judicial acumen or decision-making, which must remain with judges.The CJI cautioned that the digital divide, data security and algorithmic accountability remain common challenges for Asian constitutional courts. He said the AACC can facilitate shared learning and help courts strengthen their technological networks, while ensuring that justice remains accessible, accountable and, above all, human.

Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, today extended his warm greetings to everyone on the occasion of the birth anniversaries of Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.He said that former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan.” In today’s era, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan, Jai Vigyan, Jai Anusandhan.” He further said that Mahatma Gandhi’s message of non-violence is particularly important today.Violence has increased across the world, and in such circumstances, Gandhiji’s message of non-violence and brotherhood becomes even more relevant.He said that even after so many years, Mahatma Gandhi remains loved by people across the world because his message will always remain relevant to humanity. He prayed that Mahatma Gandhi’s dream of Ram Rajya may be established not only in Hindustan but across the entire world.

. Home Minister Amit Shah paid his obeisance to Mahatma Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary today. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that Gandhi did not consider Swaraj merely as the goal of freedom, but as the foundation of self-respect and self-reliance.He added that with the belief that no nation can become great without being connected to its roots, Mahatma Gandhi established Swadeshi, one’s own language, one’s own culture, and cleanliness as the fundamental philosophy of Indian society.Mr Shah said he taught all through his life that when there is devotion in action and purity in thoughts, no goal is impossible.The Home Minister also offered salutations to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri on his 122nd birth anniversary.  Mr Shah noted that Shastri elevated the nation’s food providers and border guardians to symbols of the country’s strength and pride with the proclamation of ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’.He added that the former Prime Minister’s resolute leadership in challenging circumstances and the bold decisions taken in the interest of the nation are etched in golden letters in India’s history.Further, the Home Minister underlined that the ideas of Lal Bahadur Shastri, who made simplicity a tradition, duty a spiritual practice, and national service the very essence of life, will forever guide the people of this country.
